item.content:encoded:
News Creator Corps Trusted Creator Fellowship is now accepting applications for its Fall 2026 Trusted Creator Fellowship, an exciting opportunity designed specifically for U.S.-based independent content creators who want to strengthen their credibility, improve their reporting skills, and better serve their online communities. Rather than focusing on traditional journalism, this fellowship supports digital creators who regularly provide valuable information to niche audiences across platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Twitch, Substack, and more.

Participants selected for this prestigious fellowship will receive intensive virtual training from experienced professionals, practical newsroom-inspired skills, access to an engaged network of creators, and a $5,000 stipend upon successful completion of the program.

Whether you create local community updates, public health information, parenting content, restaurant recommendations, educational resources, or other community-focused information, the News Creator Corps Trusted Creator Fellowship can help elevate your work while improving the quality and trustworthiness of the information you share.

What is the News Creator Corps Trusted Creator Fellowship?

The News Creator Corps Trusted Creator Fellowship is a short-term virtual fellowship program that helps independent digital creators improve the quality, reliability, and credibility of the information they produce and distribute online.

As misinformation continues to spread across digital platforms, creators increasingly play an important role in informing their communities. The fellowship recognizes this growing responsibility and equips creators with practical journalism-inspired skills that help them produce more accurate, responsible, and trustworthy content.

Unlike traditional journalism programs, this fellowship is specifically tailored for independent creators who have built engaged online communities and regularly provide information that people rely upon.

Throughout the fellowship, participants receive mentorship, professional development, collaborative learning opportunities, and practical experience that they can immediately apply to their own content.

About News Creator Corps

News Creator Corps is an initiative of the Good Information Foundation dedicated to supporting trusted creators who serve their communities through accurate, reliable, and meaningful information.

The organization believes that independent creators have become important sources of information for millions of people and seeks to strengthen this emerging ecosystem by providing education, partnerships, and professional development opportunities.

Its Trusted Creator Fellowship is one of its flagship programs designed to build a stronger network of responsible information providers across the United States.

Fellowship Benefits

Selected fellows will receive numerous benefits throughout the program, including:

  • A $5,000 stipend upon successful completion of the fellowship.
  • Weekly virtual training sessions led by experienced professionals.
  • Practical instruction in journalism-inspired reporting techniques.
  • Training on responsible information sharing.
  • Improved fact-checking skills.
  • Better interviewing techniques.
  • Stronger sourcing methods.
  • Enhanced research capabilities.
  • Opportunities to immediately apply newly learned skills to personal content platforms.
  • Access to discussion forums.
  • Networking opportunities with fellow creators.
  • Connections with trainers, News Creator Corps staff, and alumni.
  • Membership in a growing network of trusted creators.
  • Professional development that strengthens long-term credibility and audience trust.

What Will Fellows Learn?

The fellowship focuses on practical skills that improve the quality and trustworthiness of digital content.

Participants will receive training in areas such as:

Fact-Checking

Creators will learn methods for verifying information before publishing content, helping reduce misinformation and improve audience trust.

Interviewing Skills

Participants will develop stronger interviewing techniques to collect accurate, balanced, and reliable information from sources.

Responsible Sourcing

The fellowship teaches creators how to identify credible sources, evaluate information, and properly attribute content.

Information Verification

Creators will gain practical approaches for confirming the accuracy of claims before sharing them with their audiences.

Community Engagement

Participants will learn strategies for serving their communities with reliable, useful, and responsible information.

Practical Application

Throughout the fellowship, creators will apply these skills directly to the content they publish on their own digital platforms.

Who Should Apply?

The fellowship is intended for independent digital creators who already serve an engaged audience with informative content.

Ideal applicants include creators covering topics such as:

  • Local news and community updates
  • Restaurant openings and local businesses
  • Public health information
  • Parenting advice and discussions
  • Educational content
  • Community events
  • Civic information
  • Neighborhood stories
  • Local resources
  • Lifestyle information that helps communities
  • Other information-based community services

Applicants should have:

  • An engaged online audience.
  • A presence on at least one digital platform.
  • A commitment to providing useful information to a defined community.
  • A desire to improve content quality and credibility.

Eligible digital platforms include:

  • Instagram
  • TikTok
  • Twitch
  • YouTube
  • Substack
  • Other digital publishing platforms

Special Opportunity for College Students

For the Fall 2026 cohort, News Creator Corps has reserved three fellowship positions specifically for current full-time college students.

This initiative reflects the organization’s commitment to supporting younger creators who are already influencing how their peers consume information.

College-aged creators often reach audiences in their late teens and early twenties—individuals who are actively forming lifelong information habits. By investing in these creators early, the fellowship aims to strengthen trusted information ecosystems for future generations.

Student fellows will participate in the exact same fellowship experience as every other cohort member.

Who Is Not the Right Fit?

While the fellowship welcomes creators from many backgrounds, it is not intended for traditional journalists who already possess professional newsroom experience.

Individuals who have already received extensive training in:

  • Fact-checking
  • FOIA requests
  • Professional interviewing
  • News sourcing
  • Investigative reporting
  • Traditional journalism practices

are unlikely to gain significant additional value from this fellowship.

Fellowship Schedule

The Fall 2026 fellowship will run virtually over approximately two and a half months.

Participants can expect:

  • Weekly virtual cohort meetings.
  • Sessions held once each week.
  • Fellowship period running from approximately October 5 through December 18, 2026.
  • Practical assignments completed through participants’ own digital channels.
  • Ongoing collaboration with cohort members.
  • Access to online discussion communities throughout the program.

Application Process

Applicants interested in joining the fellowship should complete the online application before the stated deadline.

Applicants who are eligible as current college students may submit their applications through the dedicated student application.

Prospective applicants who are unsure whether they qualify are encouraged to apply and explain the type of content they create and the communities they serve.

Important Dates

  • Applications Open: Currently Open
  • Application Deadline: August 17, 2026 (11:59 p.m. Eastern Time)
  • Notification of Applicants: By the end of September 2026
  • Program Duration: Approximately October 5 – December 18, 2026

Why This Fellowship Matters

Independent creators have become some of today’s most influential sources of community information. As audiences increasingly turn to social media and digital platforms instead of traditional media outlets, ensuring that creators have strong verification, sourcing, and reporting skills is more important than ever.

The News Creator Corps Trusted Creator Fellowship recognizes this shift by investing directly in creators who are already making a positive impact within their communities. By combining journalism best practices with creator-focused learning, the fellowship empowers participants to build greater trust, strengthen audience relationships, and improve the quality of online information.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should submit their applications through the official News Creator Corps application portal before the deadline.

APPLY NOW

APPLY AS A COLLEGE STUDENT

Conclusion

The News Creator Corps Trusted Creator Fellowship 2026 represents an outstanding opportunity for independent U.S.-based digital creators who are passionate about serving their communities with accurate, trustworthy, and engaging information. With comprehensive virtual training, access to an experienced network of professionals and creators, practical journalism-inspired skills, and a $5,000 stipend, the fellowship provides both financial support and long-term professional development.

Whether you create local news updates, educational content, public health information, or community-focused discussions, this fellowship offers the tools needed to enhance your credibility and make an even greater impact. Interested creators should submit their applications before August 17, 2026, to be considered for the Fall 2026 cohort.

Visit the OFY Website for more Fellowship Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Digital exclusion remains one of the greatest barriers preventing communities from accessing education, employment, healthcare, government services, and economic opportunities. While technology continues to transform society, millions of people still lack reliable internet access, digital devices, or the skills needed to fully participate in the digital world. To address this growing challenge, the NTEN Digital Inclusion Fellowship 2026 has opened applications for nonprofit professionals who are passionate about building stronger, more digitally connected communities.

This prestigious year-long fellowship equips nonprofit professionals with the knowledge, practical skills, mentorship, funding support, and national professional network necessary to create sustainable digital literacy programs that directly address the needs of underserved communities.

Rather than simply providing theoretical training, the fellowship empowers participants to design, implement, and sustain innovative digital inclusion initiatives within their own organizations and communities. Fellows also receive a mini-grant to help launch or expand their projects, ensuring that the ideas developed during the fellowship become real-world solutions.

If your organization serves communities affected by digital inequality and you are looking for an opportunity to become a leader in digital inclusion, this fellowship offers the resources and support needed to make a lasting impact.

About the NTEN Digital Inclusion Fellowship

The Digital Inclusion Fellowship is a comprehensive professional development program created by NTEN to strengthen nonprofit organizations working with communities experiencing digital inequity.

The fellowship recognizes that access to technology is no longer optional—it is essential for education, employment, healthcare, financial inclusion, civic participation, and overall quality of life. However, many nonprofit organizations lack the specialized knowledge, funding, and organizational capacity needed to develop effective digital literacy initiatives.

To bridge this gap, NTEN provides fellows with structured learning, coaching, networking opportunities, practical resources, and financial assistance to build sustainable digital literacy programs that respond directly to their communities’ unique needs.

The fellowship supports organizations that already have deep relationships with underserved communities and helps them transform those relationships into meaningful digital inclusion initiatives.

Fellowship Objectives

The Digital Inclusion Fellowship seeks to:

  • Increase digital literacy across underserved communities.
  • Build sustainable digital inclusion programs.
  • Strengthen nonprofit organizational capacity.
  • Equip professionals with advanced digital inclusion expertise.
  • Promote equitable access to technology.
  • Support community-centered digital equity solutions.
  • Foster collaboration among digital inclusion leaders.
  • Encourage advocacy for policies that improve digital access.

What Fellows Will Learn

Throughout the year-long fellowship, participants receive extensive professional development covering every major aspect of digital inclusion program development.

Training areas include:

1. Digital Inclusion Best Practices

Participants gain an in-depth understanding of:

  • Digital equity principles
  • Digital inclusion strategies
  • Community-centered technology initiatives
  • Barriers to internet adoption
  • Sustainable digital literacy programming

2. Digital Literacy Education

Fellows learn how to:

  • Design digital literacy curricula
  • Teach essential computer skills
  • Improve internet navigation skills
  • Develop digital confidence among learners
  • Support learners with varying levels of digital experience

3. Adult Education

The fellowship includes instruction on:

  • Adult learning methodologies
  • Inclusive teaching practices
  • Learner engagement
  • Accessible educational approaches
  • Customized learning pathways

4. Program Management

Participants build expertise in:

  • Project planning
  • Program implementation
  • Monitoring and evaluation
  • Budget management
  • Program sustainability

5. Community Outreach and Engagement

Fellows develop practical skills to:

  • Engage underserved populations
  • Build trust within communities
  • Conduct outreach campaigns
  • Recruit program participants
  • Maintain community partnerships

6. Data Collection and Evaluation

Training includes:

  • Measuring program impact
  • Collecting meaningful data
  • Using evaluation tools
  • Reporting outcomes
  • Improving future programming

7. Partnership Development

Participants learn strategies for:

  • Building strategic partnerships
  • Collaborating with local organizations
  • Strengthening community networks
  • Working across sectors
  • Expanding program reach

8. Digital Tools

Fellows receive guidance on using digital technologies that improve:

  • Program delivery
  • Communication
  • Virtual learning
  • Participant engagement
  • Administrative efficiency

9. Advocacy and Policy

An important component of the fellowship focuses on:

  • Digital equity advocacy
  • Public policy awareness
  • Community leadership
  • Technology access initiatives
  • Long-term systemic change

Fellowship Benefits

Successful fellows receive numerous professional and organizational benefits throughout the fellowship.

Professional Training

Participants receive comprehensive training covering:

  • Digital inclusion
  • Digital literacy
  • Adult education
  • Curriculum development
  • Community engagement
  • Program leadership

Mentorship

Every fellow receives:

  • Personalized guidance
  • Expert advice
  • Professional coaching
  • Ongoing mentorship throughout the fellowship

National Network

Participants become part of an expanding community that includes:

  • Digital inclusion professionals
  • Nonprofit leaders
  • Subject matter experts
  • Organizational partners
  • Previous fellowship alumni

These relationships create opportunities for long-term collaboration beyond the fellowship year.

Practical Resources

Fellows gain access to valuable tools such as:

  • Evaluation frameworks
  • Program planning templates
  • Digital literacy toolkits
  • Sustainability resources
  • Best-practice guides

National Visibility

The fellowship provides recognition through opportunities including:

  • Speaking engagements
  • Professional webinars
  • Publications
  • Leadership showcases
  • National exposure as a digital inclusion leader

Mini-Grant Funding

Each fellowship project receives financial support through a mini-grant that can be used to:

  • Launch a new digital literacy initiative
  • Expand an existing program
  • Purchase program resources
  • Support implementation activities

The amount of funding varies depending on location.

Program Structure

Each fellow designs and implements a customized digital inclusion program specifically tailored to the needs of their organization and community.

Rather than following a one-size-fits-all approach, the fellowship encourages locally driven solutions that reflect community priorities and organizational missions.

Throughout the year, fellows receive continuous support while planning, implementing, evaluating, and refining their projects.

Fellowship Locations

The fellowship is currently offered only in selected locations across the United States and Canada, depending on available partnerships and partner service areas.

Organizations interested in expanding access may also partner with NTEN to bring the fellowship to their cities or selected locations.

Organizations may sponsor:

  • One of their own employees
  • An employee from a partner organization

Who Should Apply?

The fellowship is ideal for nonprofit professionals who:

  • Work directly with underserved communities.
  • Are passionate about digital equity.
  • Want to create sustainable digital literacy programs.
  • Seek professional development opportunities.
  • Wish to strengthen their organization’s community impact.
  • Are interested in technology access and digital inclusion.

Applicants should also have organizational support, as supervisors are required to confirm the fellow’s participation and time commitment.

Application Process

Applications for the 2026 Digital Inclusion Fellowship are currently open.

To complete an application, two separate forms must be submitted:

  1. Fellow Application Form.
  2. Supervisor Support Form confirming organizational support and time commitment.

Both forms are mandatory. Applications that do not include both submissions will not be considered.

Applicants with questions during the application process may contact NTEN through the fellowship’s designated contact person for assistance.

APPLY HERE

Why This Fellowship Matters

Digital access has become essential for participating in modern society. Without internet connectivity and digital skills, communities face increased barriers to employment, education, healthcare, entrepreneurship, and civic engagement.

The NTEN Digital Inclusion Fellowship addresses these challenges by investing in nonprofit professionals who are already trusted within their communities. Through advanced training, mentorship, funding, and practical implementation support, fellows become catalysts for long-term digital equity.

The fellowship not only benefits individual professionals but also strengthens nonprofit organizations, expands community capacity, and contributes to more equitable access to technology across underserved populations.

Visit HERE to learn more about the NTEN Digital Inclusion Fellowship 2026

Conclusion

The NTEN Digital Inclusion Fellowship 2026 offers a unique opportunity for nonprofit professionals to become leaders in digital equity while creating sustainable solutions for communities affected by the digital divide. Combining year-long professional development, expert mentorship, national networking opportunities, practical implementation resources, and project funding, the fellowship equips participants with everything they need to design impactful digital literacy programs.

Organizations committed to reducing digital inequality should strongly consider supporting eligible staff members to apply. By participating in this fellowship, professionals can strengthen their leadership skills, expand their networks, secure funding for community initiatives, and make lasting contributions toward building more digitally inclusive communities.

Deadline: Applications are currently open. No specific application deadline has been announced in the provided information. Interested applicants are encouraged to complete application of the fellowship  by August 31, 2026, for early review and will remain open until filled..

For more global fellowship oppportunities visit OFY HERE

item.content:encoded:
Conciliation Resources Programme Manager (West Africa Programme) Consultant applications are now open for experienced professionals passionate about peacebuilding, governance, conflict transformation, and international development in West Africa. This five-month fixed-term consultancy, based in Accra, Ghana, offers a unique opportunity to contribute to regional peacebuilding initiatives while supporting strategic programmes across multiple West African countries.

The successful candidate will join Conciliation Resources’ West Africa Programme (WAP), working alongside regional partners, international experts, and local peacebuilding organizations to strengthen dialogue, governance, conflict prevention, and sustainable peace across some of West Africa’s most conflict-affected regions.

If you have experience in programme management, project administration, monitoring and evaluation, financial management, and peacebuilding, this role provides an excellent opportunity to make a meaningful impact while expanding your career within an internationally respected peacebuilding organization.

About Conciliation Resources

Conciliation Resources is an independent international peacebuilding organization committed to preventing violence, resolving conflicts, and promoting sustainable peace across the world.

The organization believes that lasting peace cannot be achieved overnight. Instead, sustainable peace requires:

  • Long-term partnerships
  • Inclusive dialogue
  • Community participation
  • Practical conflict resolution
  • Local ownership of peace processes

Rather than imposing external solutions, Conciliation Resources works alongside communities affected by violent conflict, helping local actors develop lasting solutions that address the root causes of instability.

Today, the organization employs more than 80 full-time and part-time staff located primarily across:

  • United Kingdom
  • Australia
  • Kenya
  • Ethiopia

Additionally, Conciliation Resources collaborates with more than 70 local and international partner organizations across multiple countries.

About the West Africa Programme

The West Africa Programme (WAP) plays a critical role in advancing peacebuilding and governance initiatives across one of Africa’s most dynamic and complex regions.

Its work focuses on promoting:

  • Inclusive peacebuilding
  • Conflict prevention
  • Dialogue and mediation
  • Good governance
  • Youth participation
  • Community resilience

The programme operates through a strong partnership model, working closely with local organizations, government institutions, civil society groups, and regional stakeholders.

Current programme activities include projects across:

  • Burkina Faso
  • Côte d’Ivoire
  • Ghana
  • Nigeria

The programme also supports peacebuilding initiatives across:

  • Cross-border communities
  • National governance structures
  • Local peace committees
  • Community dialogue mechanisms

Special emphasis is placed on addressing the root causes of conflict while strengthening long-term governance systems.

Position Overview

The successful candidate will serve as the Programme Manager (West Africa Programme) on a five-month fixed-term contract covering a period of paternity leave.

Although temporary, the role carries significant responsibility in ensuring the successful implementation and coordination of ongoing peacebuilding programmes.

The Programme Manager will provide:

  • Programmatic support
  • Administrative coordination
  • Analytical research
  • Partner engagement
  • Project management
  • Financial support
  • Monitoring and reporting

The role serves as a bridge between regional partners and the broader West Africa Programme team.

Location

The position is based in:

Accra, Ghana

Applicants must already possess the legal right to live and work in Ghana.

Contract Duration

  • Fixed-term consultancy
  • Five months
  • Paternity cover

Reporting Structure

The Programme Manager will report directly to:

  • Programme Director, West Africa Programme

The successful candidate will work closely with:

  • Programme Officer
  • Africa Department
  • London-based teams
  • Regional consultants
  • Local partners
  • Volunteers supporting programme delivery

Key Responsibilities

The Programme Manager will support the implementation of multiple regional peacebuilding initiatives while ensuring smooth programme coordination.

Responsibilities include:

1. Programme Management

The successful candidate will:

  • Coordinate programme activities
  • Support implementation across multiple projects
  • Ensure smooth programme delivery
  • Maintain communication between partners and programme staff
  • Monitor programme progress

2. Partner Coordination

A major part of the role involves working with local and international partners by:

  • Building collaborative relationships
  • Supporting project implementation
  • Coordinating activities
  • Maintaining communication
  • Providing administrative support

The Programme Manager will work with partners throughout:

  • Ghana
  • Burkina Faso
  • Côte d’Ivoire
  • Northeast Nigeria

3. Regional Analysis

The successful candidate will contribute policy and strategic analysis concerning:

  • Alliance of Sahel States (AES)
  • Nigeria
  • Mano River Union
  • Regional governance
  • Political developments
  • Conflict dynamics
  • Security trends
  • Youth participation in peacebuilding

These analyses will help shape programme strategy and policy recommendations.

4. Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL)

Responsibilities include supporting:

  • Project monitoring
  • Programme evaluation
  • Progress reporting
  • Learning processes
  • Documentation
  • Results tracking

The Programme Manager will help ensure that projects demonstrate measurable outcomes and lessons learned.

5. Financial Support

Financial responsibilities include assisting with:

  • Budget preparation
  • Financial monitoring
  • Expenditure tracking
  • Financial reporting

6. Report Writing

The role requires preparing and contributing to:

  • Programme reports
  • Analytical papers
  • Policy briefs
  • Internal documentation
  • Donor reporting

Strong written communication skills are therefore essential.

7. Administrative Coordination

The Programme Manager will support the efficient operation of the programme through:

  • Administrative management
  • Information management
  • Database maintenance
  • Documentation
  • Scheduling
  • Coordination across offices

Regional Focus Areas

The Programme covers important geopolitical areas including:

  • Burkina Faso
  • Ghana
  • Côte d’Ivoire
  • Northeast Nigeria
  • Alliance of Sahel States
  • Mano River Union

Candidates should possess a strong understanding of current political and security developments affecting these regions.

Commitment to Safeguarding

Conciliation Resources places safeguarding at the centre of all its operations.

The Programme Manager will contribute by:

  • Promoting a positive safeguarding culture
  • Supporting safeguarding implementation
  • Helping protect colleagues and programme participants
  • Maintaining safe working practices across programme activities

Essential Qualifications and Experience

Applicants should possess experience in:

  • Programme management
  • International development
  • Peacebuilding
  • Humanitarian programming
  • Project administration

Candidates should also demonstrate experience in:

  • Financial management
  • Budget preparation
  • Monitoring and evaluation
  • Project reporting
  • Analytical writing
  • Partner coordination
  • Programme implementation

Required Knowledge

Applicants should possess strong knowledge of:

  • Peacebuilding
  • Conflict transformation
  • Governance
  • Political developments in West Africa
  • Alliance of Sahel States (AES)
  • Nigeria
  • Mano River Union
  • Youth-focused peacebuilding

Required Skills

Successful candidates should demonstrate:

  • Excellent organizational skills
  • Strong analytical ability
  • Report writing
  • Communication skills
  • Project coordination
  • Administrative management
  • Problem-solving
  • Initiative
  • Political awareness
  • Cross-cultural sensitivity

Applicants must also have excellent working knowledge of:

  • Microsoft Office
  • Email systems
  • Databases
  • Internet research

Language Requirements

Applicants must have:

  • Excellent spoken English
  • Excellent written English

Working knowledge of French is highly desirable.

Knowledge of local languages spoken across the tri-border area and northeast Nigeria is considered an advantage.

Desirable Experience

Additional advantages include experience with:

  • Policy analysis
  • Background research
  • Briefing papers
  • Peacebuilding research
  • Outcome Harvesting
  • Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) methodologies

Travel Requirements

The role requires:

  • Occasional irregular working hours
  • Regional travel across West Africa when necessary

Right to Work

Applicants must already have the legal right to live and work in Ghana.

How to Apply

Applicants should note that Conciliation Resources has a specific application process.

Do not submit a CV or résumé during the initial application stage.

Instead:

  1. Download the Job Description.
  2. Download the Application Form.
  3. Download the Application Statement.
  4. Complete all required application documents.
  5. Submit the completed documents via email to recruitment@c-r.org before the application deadline.

Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by:

17:00 UK Time, Monday, 3 August 2026

Late applications may not be considered.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

Working with Conciliation Resources offers professionals the opportunity to contribute directly to peacebuilding efforts across one of Africa’s most strategically important regions.

This consultancy provides valuable experience in:

  • International peacebuilding
  • Regional governance
  • Conflict prevention
  • Programme management
  • Strategic policy analysis
  • Partnership development
  • International development programming

Professionals interested in long-term careers with NGOs, multilateral organizations, humanitarian agencies, or peacebuilding institutions will find this role particularly valuable.

Conclusion

The Conciliation Resources Programme Manager (West Africa Programme) Consultant position presents an outstanding opportunity for experienced peacebuilding and international development professionals seeking to contribute to conflict prevention and sustainable peace across West Africa.

Working from Accra, Ghana, the successful candidate will support strategic programmes spanning Ghana, Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, and Nigeria while collaborating with regional partners and international teams. Through programme coordination, policy analysis, financial oversight, monitoring and evaluation, and partner engagement, the Programme Manager will play a central role in advancing inclusive governance and long-term peacebuilding initiatives.

Interested candidates who meet the eligibility requirements are encouraged to complete the official application documents and submit them before the closing deadline.

Visit the OFY website for more Job Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Wisconsin–Madison is accepting applications for an Assistant Professor of Public Policy position focused on “Market-Based Solutions to Societal Challenges.” The appointment will be based at the university’s La Follette School of Public Affairs within the College of Letters & Science in Madison, Wisconsin.

This opportunity is intended for an academically accomplished scholar whose research investigates how markets, competitive arrangements, incentives, property rights, institutional structures, and carefully designed public policies can be used to address complex social and economic problems.

The selected scholar will be expected to conduct theoretically grounded and empirically rigorous research, contribute to public policy teaching and student mentoring, participate in interdisciplinary collaboration, and support the wider academic and service mission of the La Follette School and the College of Letters & Science.

Important Details at a Glance

  • Position title: Assistant Professor of Public Policy — Market-Based Solutions to Societal Challenges
  • Requisition number: JR10012581
  • Institution: University of Wisconsin–Madison
  • School: La Follette School of Public Affairs
  • College: College of Letters & Science
  • Location: Madison, Wisconsin, United States
  • Work arrangement: On-site
  • Employment type: Regular
  • Position profile: Assistant Professor
  • Appointment basis: Academic, nine-month appointment
  • Compensation: Negotiable
  • Full-consideration deadline: October 18, 2026, at 11:59 p.m.
  • Final closing arrangement: Applications may continue to be accepted until the position is filled
  • Employment sponsorship: Not available
  • Application method: Online through the UW–Madison employment system

The university’s official posting identifies the appointment as regular, on-site faculty employment on a nine-month academic compensation basis. It does not publish a fixed salary range; compensation will be negotiated with the successful candidate.

About the La Follette School of Public Affairs

The Robert M. La Follette School of Public Affairs is part of the University of Wisconsin–Madison and is situated within the College of Letters & Science. The school focuses on strengthening the design, implementation, and evaluation of public policy and improving the practice of governance.

Its broader mission emphasizes evidence-based policymaking, interdisciplinary research, public engagement, and the advancement of the public good. La Follette students and faculty also collaborate with government institutions, nonprofit organizations, private-sector entities, and other stakeholders to address real-world public policy challenges.

The College of Letters & Science is home to 39 academic departments and a wide range of research centers. The successful candidate will therefore join a broad intellectual community with potential opportunities for collaboration across multiple disciplines, departments, and policy research initiatives.

Purpose of the Assistant Professor Position

Through this appointment, the La Follette School seeks to recruit a scholar who can examine the potential of market-based institutions and incentive-compatible public policies to address major societal challenges.

The successful candidate’s research should explore the role of markets in areas that have traditionally been influenced by:

  • Government policy;
  • Economic and social regulation;
  • Public-sector intervention;
  • Institutional limitations;
  • Market failure;
  • Government failure;
  • Collective action problems; and
  • The need to coordinate individuals, firms, communities, and public institutions.

The school is particularly interested in research that evaluates how market mechanisms operate, when they produce socially beneficial results, where they fail, and how institutional or policy reforms can improve their performance.

Research should be both theoretically informed and empirically rigorous. This means that applicants should be capable of connecting economic, legal, political, institutional, or public policy theory with credible evidence and appropriate research methods.

Core Research Themes

The successful candidate may examine how the following concepts affect public policy and societal outcomes:

Prices

Research may consider how prices communicate information, influence behavior, allocate scarce resources, or create incentives for individuals and organizations.

Relevant work may also examine the limitations of pricing systems, including situations involving externalities, unequal access, concentrated market power, incomplete information, or public goods.

Property Rights

Applicants may study how the design, allocation, enforcement, or reform of property rights affects investment, resource use, innovation, environmental protection, housing development, agricultural production, or economic participation.

Competition

Research may investigate how competitive structures influence service quality, affordability, productivity, consumer welfare, innovation, institutional performance, or the distribution of economic opportunities.

Decentralized Information

Scholars may analyze how information dispersed among individuals, firms, governments, and communities can be incorporated into policy design and institutional decision-making.

Institutional Design

The appointment is particularly relevant to researchers studying how laws, regulations, governance structures, administrative systems, contractual arrangements, or market rules shape behavior and public outcomes.

Incentive-Compatible Policy Design

Candidates may examine how policies can be structured so that the incentives of individuals, organizations, public authorities, and private firms support the intended public policy objectives rather than undermining them.

Priority Public Policy Areas

The La Follette School has identified several substantive areas of interest. Applicants do not necessarily need to cover every area, but their research should demonstrate a strong connection to markets, incentives, competition, institutional design, or related economic principles.

1. Education, School Finance, and School Choice

Relevant research may explore:

  • School funding models;
  • Education vouchers;
  • Charter schools;
  • Competition among educational institutions;
  • Incentives for teachers and administrators;
  • Resource allocation in education;
  • Parental choice;
  • Access and equity implications; and
  • The effects of alternative education financing arrangements.

2. Financial Regulation and Capital Markets

Research could address:

  • Banking regulation;
  • Financial market competition;
  • Consumer financial protection;
  • Capital allocation;
  • Securities regulation;
  • Financial stability;
  • Market transparency;
  • Risk incentives;
  • Corporate governance; and
  • The relationship between regulation and financial innovation.

3. Housing Supply and Land-Use Reform

Candidates may investigate:

  • Housing affordability;
  • Zoning and land-use regulation;
  • Barriers to housing construction;
  • Property development incentives;
  • Urban growth;
  • Rent and ownership markets;
  • Housing finance;
  • Local government regulation; and
  • Reforms intended to increase housing supply.

4. Technology Policy and Innovation Markets

Potential topics may include:

  • Technology regulation;
  • Competition policy;
  • Digital markets;
  • Intellectual property;
  • Innovation incentives;
  • Platform governance;
  • Artificial intelligence policy;
  • Data governance;
  • Market concentration; and
  • The relationship between regulation and technological development.

5. Transportation and Infrastructure Finance

Relevant areas may include:

  • Road pricing;
  • Public-private partnerships;
  • Transportation markets;
  • Infrastructure investment;
  • User-fee models;
  • Public transit finance;
  • Congestion pricing;
  • Project financing;
  • Infrastructure regulation; and
  • Incentives for efficient infrastructure use.

6. International Trade and Tariffs

Scholars may examine:

  • Tariff policy;
  • Trade restrictions;
  • Global supply chains;
  • International competition;
  • Trade agreements;
  • Industrial policy;
  • Distributional effects of trade;
  • Market access; and
  • The political economy of international trade.

7. State and Local Economic Development

Potential research areas include:

  • Local business incentives;
  • Tax incentives;
  • Regional economic development;
  • Public investment;
  • Business attraction strategies;
  • Employment creation;
  • Urban and rural development;
  • Local government competition; and
  • Evaluation of economic development programs.

8. Climate and Environmental Policy

The announcement specifically identifies market-oriented environmental mechanisms such as:

  • Carbon pricing;
  • Cap-and-trade systems;
  • Emissions trading;
  • Environmental taxes;
  • Pollution permits;
  • Conservation incentives;
  • Climate finance;
  • Market-based environmental regulation; and
  • Institutional mechanisms for addressing environmental externalities.

9. Energy Markets and Grid Reform

Applicants may research:

  • Electricity market design;
  • Energy pricing;
  • Renewable energy incentives;
  • Grid modernization;
  • Energy competition;
  • Utility regulation;
  • Distributed energy resources;
  • Energy reliability;
  • Market integration; and
  • Reforms supporting efficient and sustainable energy systems.

10. Agricultural Policy and Food Systems

Relevant work may involve:

  • Agricultural subsidies;
  • Food market regulation;
  • Farm incentives;
  • Commodity markets;
  • Food security;
  • Agricultural insurance;
  • Rural economic development;
  • Environmental effects of agriculture;
  • Supply-chain competition; and
  • Institutional reforms affecting food systems.

Academic Disciplines Considered

The position is intentionally interdisciplinary. The La Follette School may consider candidates from several academic traditions, including:

  • Economics;
  • Political science;
  • Public policy;
  • Public administration;
  • Law;
  • Sociology; and
  • Other affiliated social science disciplines.

A candidate’s formal disciplinary title is less important than the substance of the research. The applicant’s scholarship should engage seriously with the economic logic of markets, incentives, competition, institutional structures, and public policy design.

Research Methods Welcomed

The school welcomes candidates using diverse methodological approaches. Appropriate research methods may include:

Structural Modelling

Structural modelling may be used to estimate behavioral relationships, test theoretical mechanisms, simulate policy reforms, or evaluate how individuals and organizations respond to changes in prices, incentives, regulations, or institutional arrangements.

Reduced-Form Econometrics

Candidates may use quasi-experimental and other econometric techniques to estimate causal or empirical relationships between policies, institutions, markets, and societal outcomes.

Field Experiments

Researchers may conduct randomized or carefully designed field experiments to test incentives, policy interventions, institutional mechanisms, or behavioral responses in real-world settings.

Institutional Analysis

Institutional research may evaluate how formal rules, informal norms, legal structures, governance arrangements, or administrative systems influence policy performance.

Political Economy Frameworks

Political economy research may examine how political institutions, interest groups, government incentives, public decision-making, and economic structures interact to shape public policy outcomes.

The listing of these approaches is not necessarily exhaustive. The central requirement is that the candidate’s methods should be appropriate for producing credible, analytically sound, and policy-relevant research.

Teaching Responsibilities

The selected Assistant Professor will contribute to the La Follette School’s teaching mission. Expected teaching areas may include:

  • Public policy analysis;
  • Microeconomics for public policy;
  • Regulatory policy;
  • Market and institutional analysis;
  • Sector-specific public policy courses; and
  • Other courses aligned with the candidate’s expertise.

The successful candidate will help students understand:

  • When markets function effectively;
  • Why markets sometimes fail;
  • How public policy can improve market performance;
  • How regulations and institutions affect incentives;
  • How government interventions should be evaluated; and
  • How government failure can create persistent risks for policy implementation.

Teaching should be evidence-based, student-centered, carefully planned, and responsive to the academic and professional development needs of students.

Student Mentoring Expectations

Student mentoring is a central component of the position. The successful candidate must demonstrate a commitment to creating a teaching and mentoring environment in which students can learn, develop, and thrive.

The application should show how the candidate approaches mentoring, including the goals, actions, reflection, and documentation used to support student development.

Applicants should not rely only on testimonials or letters written by other people to demonstrate their teaching and mentoring capabilities. Their own application materials must directly explain and provide evidence of their approach. Supporting letters may be included, but they cannot serve as the sole evidence.

Research and Institutional Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be expected to:

  1. Develop and maintain a productive research program.
  2. Produce theoretically grounded and empirically credible scholarship.
  3. Contribute to teaching in public policy and related subjects.
  4. Mentor students through evidence-based and student-centered practices.
  5. Collaborate with scholars across disciplines.
  6. Engage with relevant university research centers.
  7. Contribute to departmental and school activities.
  8. Participate appropriately in academic service.
  9. Support an environment in which faculty, staff, students, and community members can engage and thrive.
  10. Advance the College of Letters & Science’s educational and institutional mission.

The university expects the successful candidate to pursue important questions, contribute new knowledge, produce an impact within their field, and participate in the institution’s shared governance and academic community.

Required Educational Qualification

Applicants must possess a Ph.D. by the start of the appointment.

Acceptable fields include:

  • Public Policy;
  • Public Administration;
  • Political Science;
  • Law;
  • Economics;
  • Sociology; or
  • A closely related discipline.

Candidates who are still completing their doctoral studies may therefore be considered, provided that all requirements for the Ph.D. will be completed by the appointment’s starting date.

Required Professional and Academic Qualifications

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Excellence in research;
  • Evidence of research productivity;
  • A strong commitment to teaching;
  • A commitment to student mentoring;
  • The ability to create effective teaching and learning environments;
  • The ability to contribute positively to a departmental research environment;
  • Potential for interdisciplinary collaboration;
  • Capacity to work with scholars from other departments;
  • Potential to engage with university research centers; and
  • Evidence that their background and scholarly agenda align with the position’s market-based public policy focus.

Application materials should contain specific evidence rather than unsupported claims. Candidates should explain their qualifications through research outputs, teaching experience, mentoring practices, academic achievements, and a clearly articulated future research agenda.

Employment Location and Work Arrangement

The position is based in Madison, Wisconsin, and is designated as on-site. Candidates should therefore expect to undertake their teaching, research, mentoring, service, and institutional responsibilities in Madison rather than as a fully remote appointment.

Madison is the capital of Wisconsin. The university describes the city as combining the atmosphere of a smaller community with the facilities and cultural opportunities of a medium-sized city. The area is also recognized for its natural surroundings, schools, cultural activities, and outdoor recreation.

Compensation and Appointment Structure

The compensation is listed as:

  • Negotiable;
  • Academic; and
  • Based on a nine-month appointment.

The official announcement does not provide a fixed salary amount or salary range. Compensation will therefore be determined through the university’s appointment and negotiation process.

UW–Madison generally participates in the Wisconsin Retirement System and provides eligible faculty members with access to applicable university employee benefit arrangements. Final benefit eligibility, enrolment conditions, coverage, and deadlines should be confirmed directly through UW–Madison Human Resources.

United States Employment Eligibility Requirement

The successful applicant must be eligible for employment in the United States on or before the effective date of the appointment.

UW–Madison has clearly stated that university sponsorship is not available for this position. Applicants who would require the university to sponsor an employment visa should take this restriction into account before applying.

International scholars who already have independent authorization to work in the United States may still be eligible, subject to their individual immigration and employment circumstances. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that they can satisfy the employment eligibility requirement by the appointment date.

Application Documents Required

Applicants must submit four principal documents:

1. Letter of Application

The application letter should explain:

  • The candidate’s interest in the position;
  • Alignment between the candidate’s research and market-based policy solutions;
  • Relevant academic and research experience;
  • Potential contributions to the La Follette School;
  • Teaching interests;
  • Interdisciplinary collaboration potential; and
  • The candidate’s future research agenda.

2. Curriculum Vitae

The curriculum vitae should provide a comprehensive record of:

  • Academic qualifications;
  • Research appointments;
  • Publications;
  • Working papers;
  • Teaching experience;
  • Conference presentations;
  • Research grants;
  • Awards and distinctions;
  • Student supervision or mentoring;
  • Institutional service; and
  • Other relevant professional activities.

3. Teaching and Mentoring Statement

The teaching and mentoring statement should explain the candidate’s philosophy, methods, evidence, and future plans.

The statement should demonstrate purposeful planning through:

  • Clear teaching goals;
  • Specific classroom practices;
  • Mentoring strategies;
  • Action plans;
  • Reflection on teaching effectiveness;
  • Evidence of student-centered teaching;
  • Methods for supporting student development; and
  • Relevant documentation or examples.

The university emphasizes that this part of the application must be created by the applicant. It cannot consist only of recommendations, testimonials, or statements written by others.

4. Job Market Paper

Applicants must submit a job market paper demonstrating the quality, relevance, rigor, and potential contribution of their research.

A strong paper should allow the selection committee to assess:

  • The candidate’s theoretical contribution;
  • Research methodology;
  • Empirical credibility;
  • Understanding of markets and institutions;
  • Policy relevance;
  • Clarity of argument;
  • Quality of evidence; and
  • Potential for future scholarly productivity.

Reference Letter Process

Applicants are not instructed to upload the three reference letters as part of the initial four-item application package.

After submitting the application, each applicant will receive an email requesting:

  • The names of three references; and
  • The contact information of those three references.

Each nominated reference will then receive an electronic link through which they can upload a signed reference letter.

Applicants should select references who can provide substantive evidence regarding their research quality, teaching ability, mentoring experience, academic potential, professional conduct, and suitability for an interdisciplinary public affairs school.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted through the official UW–Madison online application system.

Applicants should:

  1. Open the official position announcement.
  2. Select the “Apply Now” option.
  3. Follow the appropriate application route for current or external employees.
  4. Complete all required personal and employment information.
  5. Upload the letter of application.
  6. Upload the curriculum vitae.
  7. Upload the teaching and mentoring statement.
  8. Upload the job market paper.
  9. Review all uploaded documents carefully.
  10. Submit the application through the online system.
  11. Monitor email for the request to provide three references.
  12. Ensure that the nominated referees submit their signed letters.

Applications sent by email, post, or through a system other than the UW–Madison online portal will not be considered.

Current employees of any Universities of Wisconsin institution must use the internal Workday application process and search for requisition number JR10012581 in the Workday Jobs Hub.

Application Deadline

For full consideration, all application materials must be received no later than:

October 18, 2026, at 11:59 p.m.

This is the full-consideration deadline rather than an absolute guarantee that the portal will close immediately afterward. The university states that applications may continue to be accepted until the position has been filled.

Applicants should nevertheless submit the complete application, including carefully prepared documents, before October 18, 2026, to ensure full consideration by the selection committee.

How Applications Will Be Evaluated

The university will evaluate candidates on the basis of the materials submitted through the application system.

Applicants should ensure that their documents directly demonstrate:

  • Research excellence;
  • Research productivity;
  • Theoretical strength;
  • Empirical rigor;
  • Alignment with the market-based policy theme;
  • Commitment to teaching;
  • Commitment to mentoring;
  • Capacity for student-centered instruction;
  • Purposeful teaching practices;
  • Interdisciplinary collaboration potential;
  • Relevant methodological expertise; and
  • Ability to contribute to the La Follette School and College of Letters & Science.

Candidates should avoid submitting generic documents that could be used for any university position. Each document should be tailored to the specific themes identified in the announcement, particularly markets, incentives, competition, decentralized information, institutional design, government failure, regulation, and major societal challenges.

Practical Guidance for Preparing a Competitive Application

A competitive applicant should explicitly connect their scholarship with the position’s central intellectual questions.

The letter and research materials should explain:

  1. What societal challenge the candidate studies.
  2. What market, institution, regulation, or incentive structure is involved.
  3. Why the issue is important for public policy.
  4. What theoretical framework guides the research.
  5. What evidence or methodology is used.
  6. What the research reveals about market success or market failure.
  7. Whether government action improves or worsens the outcome.
  8. What institutional or policy reform may be appropriate.
  9. How the research agenda could develop at UW–Madison.
  10. How collaboration with other departments or research centers would strengthen the work.

The teaching statement should go beyond broad declarations about valuing students. It should provide concrete evidence of how the applicant designs courses, communicates complex ideas, evaluates learning, mentors students, reflects on outcomes, and adjusts teaching practices.

Applicants should also make the job market paper accessible to an interdisciplinary committee. Technical rigor is important, but the paper should clearly communicate its public policy relevance, central findings, methodological contribution, and implications for markets or institutional design.

Equal Opportunity and Inclusive Recruitment

The University of Wisconsin–Madison describes diversity as a source of institutional strength, creativity, and innovation. The university seeks to create a welcoming community and recognizes the value of different identities, cultures, backgrounds, experiences, abilities, and perspectives.

Qualified applicants will receive employment consideration without discrimination on grounds including:

  • Race;
  • Color;
  • Religion;
  • Sex;
  • Sexual orientation;
  • National origin;
  • Age;
  • Pregnancy;
  • Disability;
  • Protected veteran status; and
  • Other protected grounds recognized under applicable federal regulations and University of Wisconsin System policies.

Disability and Pregnancy-Related Accommodations

Applicants who require a disability-related or pregnancy-related accommodation during any stage of the recruitment process may contact the appropriate Divisional Disability Representative.

Accommodations may be requested for stages such as:

  • Completing the application;
  • Participating in interviews;
  • Undertaking pre-employment testing; or
  • Completing other recruitment requirements.

The university recommends submitting accommodation requests as early as possible so that they can be handled effectively.

Background Checks and Reference Inquiries

Employment may be subject to a criminal background check.

References may also be asked to respond to questions concerning professional misconduct, including matters related to sexual violence or sexual harassment.

Applicants should therefore ensure that all information submitted during the recruitment process is accurate, complete, and consistent with their academic and employment records.

Applicant Confidentiality

Under the applicable Wisconsin statutory framework, the University of Wisconsin System will generally not disclose the identities of applicants who submit a written confidentiality request.

However, the identity of the person ultimately selected for the position will be released. Applicants concerned about confidentiality should review the relevant university procedure and submit any request in the required form.

Contact Information

Questions about the position or recruitment process may be directed to:

Kayla Graser
HR Generalist
University of Wisconsin–Madison
Email: kayla.graser@wisc.edu

Applicants should use the official contact for legitimate questions that are not already answered in the announcement or application portal.

Why This Academic Opportunity Is Significant

This appointment offers a scholar the opportunity to work at the intersection of economic reasoning, institutional analysis, public policy, regulation, and real-world societal challenges.

It is particularly relevant to researchers seeking to understand not merely whether government should intervene in a policy area, but how markets and governments interact, when either arrangement fails, and how better-designed institutions can improve outcomes.

The breadth of eligible policy areas allows candidates to develop research agendas in fields ranging from education and housing to trade, technology, climate policy, energy systems, infrastructure, financial regulation, agriculture, and local economic development.

At the same time, the interdisciplinary structure of the La Follette School and the wider College of Letters & Science creates scope for collaboration with economists, political scientists, sociologists, legal scholars, public affairs specialists, and researchers working in sector-specific policy fields.

Conclusion

The University of Wisconsin–Madison Assistant Professor of Public Policy position represents a substantial academic opportunity for a scholar conducting rigorous research on market institutions, competition, incentives, regulation, and institutional design.

The successful candidate will join the La Follette School of Public Affairs and contribute to research, teaching, student mentoring, interdisciplinary collaboration, and academic service. Candidates may come from economics, public policy, political science, law, sociology, public administration, or another closely related discipline, but they must possess a Ph.D. by the appointment date and demonstrate excellence in research and commitment to teaching.

Applicants must submit a letter of application, curriculum vitae, teaching and mentoring statement, and job market paper through the UW–Madison online recruitment system. Three references will be requested electronically after the initial application has been submitted.

For full consideration, complete materials must be received by 11:59 p.m. on October 18, 2026. Applications may remain open until the position is filled, but candidates should not treat that possibility as an extension of the priority deadline.

Prospective international applicants should pay particular attention to the employment authorization condition. Although the announcement does not restrict applicants by nationality, UW–Madison will not provide employment sponsorship for this appointment. Only candidates who can meet the United States employment eligibility requirement by the effective date should proceed with an application.

For more global opportunities, click HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The Green Mentorship Programme is inviting senior university students and recent graduates to participate in an exciting career development session designed to help aspiring sustainability professionals begin their journey in one of the world’s fastest-growing sectors. If you are passionate about sustainability, climate change, environmental protection, and sustainable development, this programme offers an excellent opportunity to gain valuable insights into career pathways while learning directly from professionals working in the field.

As governments, businesses, and international organizations continue to prioritize environmental sustainability and climate resilience, the demand for professionals equipped with sustainability knowledge is increasing rapidly. The Green Mentorship Programme has been created to bridge the gap between academic learning and professional practice by introducing participants to the skills, knowledge, and opportunities needed to succeed in the sustainability sector.

Whether your goal is to work with international organizations, environmental NGOs, private companies, research institutions, or public sector agencies, this mentorship session can help you better understand the industry and prepare for future career opportunities.

About the Green Mentorship Programme

The Green Mentorship Programme is a career-focused initiative designed to support students and recent graduates who want to build successful careers in sustainability and climate action.

The programme provides participants with an opportunity to learn about emerging sustainability trends, explore career options, and gain practical advice on entering this competitive and impactful field.

Rather than focusing only on theoretical knowledge, the programme emphasizes practical guidance that can help participants confidently navigate the transition from university to professional employment within the sustainability sector.

Why Sustainability Careers Matter

Sustainability has become one of the most important global priorities across industries. Organizations around the world are investing heavily in environmental protection, renewable energy, climate adaptation, sustainable development, and responsible business practices.

As a result, professionals with sustainability knowledge are increasingly sought after in sectors such as:

  • Environmental consulting
  • Renewable energy
  • Climate policy
  • Corporate sustainability
  • Sustainable finance
  • International development
  • Green technology
  • Circular economy initiatives
  • Environmental education
  • Non-governmental organizations (NGOs)
  • Government agencies
  • Research institutions

The Green Mentorship Programme aims to prepare young professionals to take advantage of these growing opportunities.

What Participants Will Learn

During the mentorship session, participants will gain valuable knowledge and practical insights into the sustainability industry.

Key learning areas include:

1. Introduction to Sustainability

Participants will explore important sustainability concepts and understand why environmental and social sustainability are becoming essential across industries.

2. Climate Change and Global Development

The programme will examine how climate change is influencing economies, societies, businesses, and international development efforts.

3. Emerging Career Opportunities

Attendees will discover various career pathways available in sustainability, including opportunities in the public sector, private companies, nonprofit organizations, and international institutions.

4. Practical Career Guidance

Participants will receive useful advice on:

  • Starting a sustainability career
  • Building relevant skills
  • Preparing for future opportunities
  • Understanding employer expectations
  • Identifying growth areas within the green economy

Benefits of Attending

Participants can expect several valuable benefits from joining the Green Mentorship Programme, including:

  • Better understanding of sustainability careers.
  • Exposure to emerging environmental and climate-related professions.
  • Practical guidance for entering the sustainability sector.
  • Increased awareness of global sustainability challenges.
  • Opportunities to connect with individuals who share similar interests.
  • Career development support for students and graduates.
  • Enhanced knowledge of sustainability and climate action.

Who Should Attend?

The programme is specifically designed for:

  • Senior university students.
  • Recent graduates.
  • Individuals interested in sustainability.
  • Young people passionate about climate action.
  • Aspiring professionals seeking careers in environmental and development sectors.

Applicants from different academic backgrounds are encouraged to participate if they have an interest in sustainability.

Session Details

Participants should note the following event information:

Location

  • Founder’s Space
  • Cairo, Egypt

Date

  • 8 August 2026

Time

  • 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM

The session will be conducted in person, providing participants with opportunities to engage directly with mentors and fellow attendees.

Why You Should Participate

Attending the Green Mentorship Programme offers an excellent opportunity to gain early exposure to one of the world’s most rapidly expanding career sectors.

By participating, you will be able to:

  • Explore sustainability career pathways.
  • Learn directly from experienced professionals.
  • Build knowledge relevant to future employment.
  • Strengthen your understanding of climate action.
  • Expand your professional network.
  • Prepare for future career opportunities in the green economy.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should complete the official registration form by providing the required information, including:

  • Full name
  • Age
  • Gender
  • Email address
  • Phone number
  • Field of study or work
  • Governorate
  • A brief response explaining what they expect to learn from the session

Applicants are encouraged to register early, as spaces for in-person events may be limited.

Application Deadline

No application deadline has been specified.

Interested participants should register as soon as possible before the session date of 8 August 2026 to secure a place.

APPLY HERE

For more mentorship programs visit OFY Website HERE

Conclusion

The Green Mentorship Programme is an excellent opportunity for senior university students and recent graduates who aspire to build meaningful careers in sustainability and climate action. Through expert guidance, practical career advice, and exposure to emerging opportunities in the green economy, participants will gain valuable insights that can help shape their professional future. If you are passionate about creating positive environmental and social impact while pursuing a rewarding career, this programme offers an ideal starting point. Register early to ensure your participation in this valuable in-person learning experience in Cairo.

item.content:encoded:
The Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (Institute for Advanced Study) has officially opened applications for its prestigious Early Career Fellowship for the 2027/2028 academic year. This internationally recognized fellowship offers early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences a unique opportunity to dedicate ten months exclusively to their own research in one of Europe’s leading interdisciplinary academic environments.

Designed to give scholars the freedom to think, write, collaborate, and develop groundbreaking ideas without the distractions of regular teaching or administrative responsibilities, the fellowship brings together researchers from different disciplines and countries to encourage intellectual exchange and innovation.

If you are an emerging researcher seeking uninterrupted time to advance your academic work while engaging with an international community of distinguished scholars, this fellowship presents an exceptional opportunity.

About the Wissenschaftskolleg Fellowship

The Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin, also known as the Institute for Advanced Study, is one of the world’s leading institutes dedicated to promoting advanced research across disciplines. Every year, it welcomes scholars from different parts of the world to pursue independent research while participating in an intellectually vibrant academic community.

Unlike many traditional research programs, the Wissenschaftskolleg places great emphasis on academic freedom. Fellows are encouraged to pursue research topics of their own choosing rather than being assigned specific institutional projects.

This approach allows researchers to explore innovative ideas, challenge existing perspectives, and produce impactful scholarship within a collaborative environment.

Fellowship Duration

Successful applicants will spend approximately 10 months at the Wissenschaftskolleg.

The fellowship runs from:

  • September 2027
  • Until the end of June 2028

Throughout this period, fellows will reside in Berlin and focus entirely on their independent research projects.

What Makes This Fellowship Unique?

One of the defining characteristics of the Wissenschaftskolleg Fellowship is its commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration.

Rather than grouping researchers only by subject area, the institute intentionally brings together scholars from different academic disciplines.

This diverse environment creates opportunities for:

  • Cross-disciplinary collaboration
  • Intellectual exchange
  • New research perspectives
  • Innovative thinking
  • Academic networking
  • International cooperation
  • Long-term scholarly partnerships

The institute believes that interactions between researchers from different fields often generate new questions, fresh approaches, and unexpected discoveries.

Freedom to Pursue Independent Research

At the heart of the fellowship is complete academic independence.

Rather than prescribing research themes, the Wissenschaftskolleg encourages fellows to develop and pursue their own research questions.

Participants can:

  • Advance ongoing research
  • Begin entirely new projects
  • Write books or journal articles
  • Complete major academic manuscripts
  • Develop interdisciplinary collaborations
  • Explore innovative methodologies

This freedom allows scholars to make meaningful contributions to their fields while benefiting from an inspiring research environment.

Fellowship Expectations

Although fellows enjoy significant academic freedom, there are a few important responsibilities.

Successful fellows are expected to:

  • Reside at the Wissenschaftskolleg throughout the fellowship period.
  • Participate in the institute’s scholarly community.
  • Join the daily communal meal, which serves as an important opportunity for informal academic discussions.
  • Attend the weekly Tuesday Colloquium where fellows present ideas, discuss research, and engage in interdisciplinary conversations.

These activities are central to the institute’s collaborative philosophy and contribute to the vibrant intellectual atmosphere experienced by all fellows.

Academic Environment

The Wissenschaftskolleg is internationally recognized for fostering a stimulating research community where scholars can exchange ideas beyond the boundaries of their individual disciplines.

Benefits of this environment include:

  • Daily interaction with internationally renowned researchers
  • Exposure to diverse academic perspectives
  • Constructive feedback on research
  • Opportunities for collaboration across disciplines
  • A supportive and intellectually engaging community
