item.content:encoded:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming every sector of society—from healthcare and education to finance, governance, agriculture, manufacturing, and scientific research. As AI systems become increasingly integrated into everyday life, ensuring that they are developed and used responsibly has become one of the world’s most pressing priorities.

Recognizing this global need, UNESCO, in partnership with LG AI Research and Coursera, has officially launched the Global MOOC on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, a free online course designed to help learners around the world understand and apply ethical principles throughout the AI lifecycle.

Announced during the Ethics by Design: Industry and Innovation Conference held in Seoul, Republic of Korea, this globally accessible Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) represents an important milestone in transforming international AI ethics standards into practical knowledge that professionals, students, policymakers, researchers, and organizations can apply in real-world situations.

Hosted on Coursera and available free of charge, the course equips learners with practical frameworks, case studies, and decision-making tools that support the responsible development, deployment, and governance of AI technologies.

About the Global MOOC on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

The Global MOOC on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence has been created to translate the principles contained in UNESCO’s Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence into practical learning experiences.

Rather than simply explaining ethical concepts, the course demonstrates how these principles can be implemented throughout every stage of AI development—from system design and model training to deployment, governance, monitoring, and long-term societal impact.

The course serves as a global public educational resource that allows learners everywhere to develop the practical skills needed to build trustworthy, transparent, fair, and human-centered AI systems.

Official Launch of the Course

The course was officially launched on 20 July 2026 during the Ethics by Design: Industry and Innovation Conference held at the Korean National Commission for UNESCO in Seoul.

The launch ceremony brought together distinguished representatives from international organizations, governments, industry, academia, and AI research communities.

Among those present were:

  • Prof. Khaled El-Enany, Director-General of UNESCO
  • Dr. Kyung Hoon Bae, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT, Republic of Korea
  • Dr. Woohyung Lim, Head of LG AI Research

The event also welcomed:

  • Government leaders
  • Technology experts
  • University researchers
  • Industry professionals
  • Members of the International Advisory Group
  • Module leaders responsible for developing the course

The gathering reflected the growing international collaboration required to ensure AI technologies remain ethical, inclusive, transparent, and beneficial to humanity.

Built on UNESCO’s Global AI Ethics Recommendation

One of the defining strengths of this MOOC is that it is based directly on the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted unanimously in 2021 by all 193 UNESCO Member States.

This Recommendation became the world’s first global normative framework dedicated specifically to AI ethics.

Rather than functioning as a theoretical document, the Recommendation establishes internationally agreed principles covering:

  • Human rights
  • Human dignity
  • Fairness
  • Transparency
  • Accountability
  • Privacy
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Inclusiveness
  • Safety
  • Responsible governance

The new course helps learners operationalize these principles in everyday professional practice.

Why This Course Matters

Artificial Intelligence is advancing rapidly across industries, creating both tremendous opportunities and significant ethical challenges.

Organizations increasingly require professionals who understand not only how AI systems work but also how they should be designed and governed responsibly.

According to UNESCO, ethical AI cannot be achieved through principles alone—it depends on people who possess the skills to apply those principles during every phase of AI development.

This course bridges the gap between policy and practice by providing learners with practical tools to:

  • Build trustworthy AI systems
  • Identify ethical risks
  • Balance innovation with responsibility
  • Protect human rights
  • Improve transparency
  • Promote accountability
  • Support inclusive AI development
  • Make informed ethical decisions

Who Should Take This Course?

The MOOC has been designed for a broad global audience.

It is suitable for:

  • Artificial intelligence professionals
  • Machine learning engineers
  • Software developers
  • AI researchers
  • Data scientists
  • University students
  • Academic researchers
  • Government policymakers
  • Public administrators
  • Technology executives
  • Product managers
  • Ethics specialists
  • Innovation leaders
  • Business professionals
  • Anyone interested in understanding responsible AI

No matter the learner’s background, the course provides practical knowledge applicable across multiple industries.

What You Will Learn

Participants will gain practical understanding of responsible AI development through ten comprehensive learning modules.

Learners will understand:

  • Ethical AI principles
  • Responsible AI design
  • Human-centered AI development
  • AI governance
  • Privacy protection
  • Transparency mechanisms
  • Risk management
  • Accountability frameworks
  • Sustainable AI practices
  • Fair AI decision-making

The course emphasizes real-world implementation rather than theoretical discussion alone.

Apply here

Course Structure: Ten Comprehensive Modules

The curriculum is organized into ten carefully designed modules covering the most important dimensions of AI ethics.

Major topics include:

1. Fairness and Inclusion

Learners explore methods for reducing bias in AI systems while promoting fairness and equitable outcomes.

Topics include:

  • Algorithmic bias
  • Inclusive datasets
  • Equal treatment
  • Social equity

2. Privacy and Data Governance

This module examines responsible data collection, management, protection, and governance.

Topics include:

  • Data privacy
  • Consent
  • Responsible data use
  • Governance policies
  • Data security

3. Transparency and Accountability

Participants learn how organizations can make AI systems understandable and accountable.

Key concepts include:

  • Explainable AI
  • Transparency reporting
  • Accountability mechanisms
  • Documentation
  • Responsible oversight

4. Safety and Security

The course explores methods for designing AI systems that remain safe, secure, and reliable.

Topics include:

  • Risk assessment
  • AI safety
  • Cybersecurity
  • System reliability
  • Responsible deployment

5. Environmental Sustainability

Learners examine how AI development affects the environment and explore strategies to reduce environmental impacts.

Topics include:

  • Energy-efficient AI
  • Sustainable computing
  • Environmental responsibility
  • Green AI practices

6. Global AI Governance

Participants study international governance models and regulatory approaches shaping AI worldwide.

Areas covered include:

  • International cooperation
  • AI regulation
  • Global standards
  • Public policy
  • Governance frameworks

7–10. Practical Ethics Throughout the AI Lifecycle

Across the remaining modules, learners engage with:

  • Practical ethical decision-making
  • Everyday AI development trade-offs
  • Real-world case studies
  • Reflection exercises
  • Ethics-by-design methodologies
  • Responsible innovation frameworks

Practical Learning Experience

Unlike many introductory AI ethics courses, this MOOC places strong emphasis on application.

Learners will work with:

  • Practical scenarios
  • Interactive exercises
  • Real-world examples
  • Reflective learning activities
  • Ethical decision-making frameworks
  • Industry case studies

The objective is to help participants confidently apply ethical principles in their own organizations and projects.

Developed Through Global Collaboration

The course represents a significant public-private partnership.

It has been co-developed by:

  • UNESCO
  • LG AI Research
  • Coursera

Its curriculum has also been shaped by independent international AI experts representing leading academic and research institutions worldwide.

This diverse collaboration ensures that the examples, perspectives, and case studies reflect different regional, cultural, and professional contexts.

Visit here for more details on UNESCO and LG AI Research Launch Free Global Ethics of Artificial Intelligence Course on Coursera

Expert Perspectives

During the launch, UNESCO Director-General Prof. Khaled El-Enany emphasized that ethical AI depends on people who can translate shared principles into everyday practice.

Dr. Kyung Hoon Bae highlighted the Republic of Korea’s commitment to supporting human-centered AI development and digital inclusion through continued collaboration with UNESCO and the international community.

Dr. Woohyung Lim of LG AI Research stressed that while international consensus on ethical AI already exists, the real challenge is embedding ethics throughout the entire AI lifecycle—from product development to operational deployment.

Coursera Chief Content Officer Marni Baker Stein noted that the platform is proud to host the course, expanding access to high-quality education on responsible AI for learners worldwide.

Industry Dialogue on Ethical AI

The launch event also featured expert panel discussions involving representatives from:

  • LG AI Research
  • United Nations University Institute in Macau
  • University of Toronto
  • Korea AI Safety Institute
  • Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology
  • Kakao
  • Naver
  • Agence Francophone et Africaine de l’Intelligence Artificielle (AFRIA)

The discussions emphasized several key priorities:

  • Building trustworthy AI
  • Strengthening AI safety
  • Improving fairness and accountability
  • Embedding ethics into everyday product development
  • Establishing strong governance structures
  • Protecting human rights
  • Communicating transparently with the public

Certification

Learners who successfully complete the course are eligible to receive a Coursera certificate, demonstrating their understanding of responsible AI and ethical AI principles.

This certificate can strengthen professional profiles for individuals working in technology, public policy, research, education, business, and digital transformation.

Language Availability

The course is delivered primarily in English.

To promote inclusive global participation, translation options are available in 11 languages, enabling learners from diverse linguistic backgrounds to benefit from the program.

Cost

The Global MOOC on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence is completely free to access through Coursera.

This makes high-quality education on AI ethics accessible to learners regardless of geographic location or financial circumstances.

Application Deadline

There is no application deadline mentioned. The course is freely available on Coursera for learners worldwide.

Why You Should Enroll

This course offers an outstanding opportunity to understand one of the most important dimensions of artificial intelligence in today’s digital world.

Whether you are building AI systems, regulating them, researching new technologies, managing AI projects, or simply seeking to understand responsible innovation, the course provides practical tools grounded in internationally recognized ethical standards.

With AI rapidly transforming industries worldwide, professionals who understand ethical AI principles will be increasingly valuable across both public and private sectors.

Conclusion

The UNESCO and LG AI Research Global MOOC on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence is more than just an online course—it is a global educational initiative aimed at ensuring AI serves humanity responsibly, fairly, and sustainably. Built upon UNESCO’s internationally recognized Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, the course transforms global ethical principles into practical skills that learners can immediately apply throughout the AI lifecycle.

Freely available through Coursera and accessible worldwide, the program offers a unique opportunity for students, professionals, policymakers, researchers, developers, and organizations to deepen their understanding of responsible AI while earning a certificate from one of the world’s leading online learning platforms. As artificial intelligence continues to reshape society, this course equips learners with the knowledge and practical frameworks needed to build trustworthy, transparent, human-centered AI systems that align innovation with ethical responsibility.

item.content:encoded:
Are you passionate about migration studies, sociology, digital platforms, labor research, or social sciences? The University of Helsinki is inviting applications for a Doctoral Researcher in the Social Sciences position under the prestigious MAPS (Mapping Fragmented Labor in the Platformised Service Sector through Migrant Epistemologies) research project. This is an excellent opportunity for aspiring researchers to pursue a fully funded doctoral project while contributing to cutting-edge research on platform work, migration, and the transformation of labor in Finland.

The position is hosted by the Swedish School of Social Sciences at the University of Helsinki and is funded by the Research Council of Finland. Successful applicants will receive funding for 3.5 years, beginning 1 October 2026, while working alongside leading researchers and completing an article-based PhD.

About the University of Helsinki Doctoral Research Position

The University of Helsinki is one of Europe’s leading research universities, known for excellence in teaching, innovation, and interdisciplinary research. This doctoral position forms part of the MAPS research project, led by Dr. Olivia Maury, which investigates how digital platforms are transforming service-sector labor through the experiences of migrant workers.

The project seeks to understand the growing influence of platform technologies on work, employment, and migration while producing new knowledge that informs policy, academia, and society.

The doctoral researcher will become part of a collaborative research environment while conducting independent doctoral research aligned with the project’s objectives.

About the MAPS Research Project

Understanding Platformized Labor Through Migration

Digital platforms have fundamentally transformed labor markets around the world. Increasingly, employment is characterized by:

  • Temporary work
  • Gig-based employment
  • Multiple job holding
  • Short-term task-based work
  • Platform-mediated employment
  • Blurred boundaries between paid and unpaid labor

The MAPS project investigates these changes by focusing specifically on migrant workers operating within Finland’s platform economy.

Rather than studying labor solely from traditional employment perspectives, the project explores how migration, digitalization, and platform technologies interact to reshape working life.

Research Focus

The project aims to understand:

  • How digital platforms reshape everyday working life.
  • How migrants experience platform-based work.
  • The relationship between migration and labor exploitation.
  • The impact of data-driven technologies on employment.
  • The influence of financial technologies on labor markets.
  • New forms of labor extraction created through digital platforms.
  • Power structures operating within platform ecosystems.

Researchers will use ethnographic methods to investigate both migrant workers’ lived experiences and the broader platform economy in Finland.

Main Responsibilities of the Doctoral Researcher

The successful candidate will undertake an independent doctoral research project while contributing to the broader MAPS research agenda.

Primary responsibilities include:

Conduct Independent Doctoral Research

The researcher will develop and complete a doctoral dissertation focused on topics including:

  • Critical migration studies
  • Sociology of work
  • Platform labor
  • Digital labor
  • Migration and employment
  • Platformization in Finland

Develop Innovative Research Methods

The researcher will participate in developing ethnographic approaches to studying:

  • Migrant workers
  • Platform companies
  • Digital labor ecosystems
  • Data-driven employment systems

Produce Academic Publications

The successful applicant will complete an article-based PhD, producing high-quality scholarly publications based on empirical research.

Participate in Project Activities

Additional responsibilities include:

  • Organizing seminars and project events
  • Participating in research communication
  • Collaborating with project members
  • Supporting dissemination of findings

Teaching Duties

The appointment includes limited teaching responsibilities, accounting for up to 5% of annual working time.

Research Areas of Interest

Applicants are encouraged to propose research that aligns with the overall project while incorporating their own academic interests and expertise.

Relevant research themes include:

  • Platform economy
  • Digital labor
  • Sociology of work
  • Migration studies
  • Ethnographic research
  • Critical migration theory
  • Platform capitalism
  • Gig economy
  • Labor precarity
  • Data-driven employment
  • Digital transformation
  • Platform governance

Who Should Apply?

The University of Helsinki welcomes applicants with strong academic backgrounds who are interested in interdisciplinary social science research.

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Strong research motivation
  • Independent thinking
  • Excellent analytical ability
  • Academic writing skills
  • Interest in migration and labor research
  • Commitment to completing a doctoral degree

The university encourages applications from individuals from diverse backgrounds and promotes an inclusive academic environment.

Eligibility Requirements

To be considered, applicants must meet the following requirements:

Educational Qualifications

Applicants should hold a Master’s degree in a field relevant to the project, such as:

  • Sociology
  • Human Geography
  • Cultural Studies
  • Social and Cultural Anthropology
  • Or another closely related discipline

Doctoral Admission

Applicants must:

  • Already have the right to pursue doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki before employment begins, or
  • Obtain doctoral study rights within the six-month probationary period.

Preferred Academic Expertise

The selection committee particularly values applicants with knowledge in one or more of the following areas:

  • Tech-finance
  • Platformization
  • Digitalization
  • Critical migration studies
  • Decolonial theory
  • Migration and labor
  • Legal theory
  • Labor law

Skills Required

Successful applicants should possess:

  • Excellent written English
  • Strong communication skills
  • Outstanding analytical abilities
  • Independent research capability
  • Motivation to conduct ethnographic research

Employment Conditions

The appointment offers a comprehensive employment package.

Key details include:

  • Fixed-term contract of 3.5 years
  • Start date: 1 October 2026
  • Six-month probation period
  • Standard Finnish pension benefits
  • Occupational healthcare
  • University employee benefits

Residence Requirement

The successful candidate is expected to reside in Finland during the employment period.

Required Application Documents

Applicants must submit the following PDF documents:

1. Motivation Letter

Maximum one page describing:

  • Interest in the project
  • Relevant background
  • Suitability for the position

2. Research Plan

Maximum two pages (including bibliography), outlining:

  • Proposed doctoral research
  • Methodology
  • Relevance to the MAPS project

3. Curriculum Vitae (CV)

A detailed academic CV highlighting:

  • Education
  • Research experience
  • Publications
  • Skills
  • Academic achievements

Click HERE to read more.

Selection Process

Applications will be evaluated based on:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Motivation
  • Research proposal
  • Previous academic performance
  • Relevant expertise
  • Interview performance

Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed during August 2026.

Important Dates

Event Date
Application Deadline 10 August 2026 (23:59 Helsinki Time)
Interviews August 2026
Employment Starts 1 October 2026
Contract Duration 3.5 Years

Why Apply?

This doctoral opportunity offers numerous advantages for aspiring researchers, including:

  • Fully funded doctoral employment
  • Research at one of Europe’s leading universities
  • Work within a prestigious Research Council of Finland project
  • Supervision by internationally recognized researchers
  • Opportunity to conduct impactful migration and labor research
  • Participation in innovative ethnographic research
  • Teaching experience
  • Access to Finland’s world-class academic environment
  • University employment benefits
  • Strong interdisciplinary research network

APPLY HERE

About the University of Helsinki

The University of Helsinki is internationally recognized for excellence in research and education. It actively promotes diversity, equality, accessibility, and inclusion while fostering innovative, interdisciplinary scholarship addressing today’s global challenges.

Researchers benefit from an intellectually stimulating environment, international collaborations, and excellent research infrastructure.

Conclusion

The Doctoral Researcher in the Social Sciences position at the University of Helsinki represents an exceptional opportunity for aspiring scholars interested in migration, sociology, digital labor, and platform studies. Through the MAPS project, successful candidates will contribute to groundbreaking research examining how digital platforms reshape labor markets and migrant experiences while earning a doctoral degree from one of Europe’s most respected universities.

With a fully funded 3.5-year appointment, strong academic mentorship, opportunities for independent research, teaching experience, and access to Finland’s outstanding research environment, this doctoral position is ideal for motivated social science graduates seeking to make meaningful contributions to the future of work, migration, and digital society.

Applicants interested in this opportunity should prepare their application materials carefully and submit them before the official deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The Greater Washington Partnership (GWP) is inviting applications for its Fall 2026 Economic Growth Internship, offering an exciting opportunity for students and recent graduates who are passionate about economic development, entrepreneurship, regional growth, innovation, and public-private collaboration. This paid internship places successful applicants at the center of one of the United States’ most influential regional economic organizations, where they will contribute to initiatives that shape the future of the Greater Washington metropolitan region.

The internship provides participants with meaningful professional experience by allowing them to work alongside policy experts, business leaders, government officials, nonprofit organizations, and economic development professionals. Interns will contribute to research, stakeholder engagement, event coordination, and strategic initiatives designed to strengthen economic competitiveness across Maryland, Virginia, and Washington, DC.

If you are looking for an internship that combines research, policy, business strategy, entrepreneurship, and regional development, this opportunity offers an outstanding platform to gain practical experience while building valuable professional networks.

About Greater Washington Partnership

The Greater Washington Partnership is a unique nonprofit alliance that brings together many of the most influential employers throughout the Greater Washington region, spanning Maryland, Virginia, and the District of Columbia.

Unlike traditional nonprofit organizations, the Partnership serves as a bridge between the public, private, and nonprofit sectors. It convenes leaders from business, government, education, and community organizations to solve regional challenges and promote sustainable economic growth.

Its mission focuses on addressing critical issues including:

  • Skills and workforce development
  • Talent attraction and retention
  • Regional transportation and mobility
  • Infrastructure development
  • Inclusive economic growth
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Innovation
  • Business competitiveness

The Partnership envisions transforming the corridor stretching from Baltimore to Richmond into one of the world’s most competitive, prosperous, and attractive places to live, work, invest, and build businesses.

About the Economic Growth Internship

The Fall 2026 Economic Growth Internship is designed for individuals interested in understanding how regional economies grow and how cross-sector partnerships influence public policy, innovation, entrepreneurship, and economic opportunity.

The internship supports implementation of the organization’s Region Rising Report, a strategic roadmap released in 2026 that outlines priorities for creating a stronger and more resilient regional economy.

Interns will become active contributors to projects that advance these priorities through research, stakeholder engagement, innovation programming, and policy support.

Rather than observing from the sidelines, interns become part of the Economic Growth team, contributing ideas and supporting projects that directly influence regional development initiatives.

  • Regional economic development

  • Tracking follow-up actions

  • Monitoring progress
  • Gathering economic insights

Tasks may include:

  • Coordinating logistics
  • Preparing event materials
  • Communicating with speakers
  • Supporting registrations
  • Assisting during live events

  • Marketing

  • Public Policy
  • Business Development
  • Events
  • Economic Growth

This interdisciplinary exposure allows interns to understand how nonprofit organizations coordinate large-scale regional initiatives.

item.content:encoded:
The Center for Global Development is recruiting a Research Analyst in London to support its work with the Smart Buys Alliance, an international collaboration focused on identifying and promoting highly cost-effective development interventions.

This full-time, mid-level position combines empirical research, quantitative analysis, policy writing, project coordination and event support. The successful candidate will help examine how bilateral donors, development agencies and governments use evidence on cost-effectiveness when making funding and policy decisions.

The Research Analyst will be based in London and is expected to work from CGD’s office at least three days each week. The position offers an annual salary of £46,725–£51,187, together with additional benefits.

The role is expected to begin as soon as possible and will initially continue until 29 February 2028. An extension may be possible, depending on the availability of funding.

Applications close on 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM British Summer Time.

CGD Research Analyst Job 2026 Overview

Key details of the opportunity include:

  • Position: Research Analyst
  • Organisation: Center for Global Development
  • Project: Smart Buys Alliance
  • Location: London, United Kingdom
  • Employment type: Full-time
  • Career level: Mid-level
  • Salary: £46,725–£51,187 per year, plus benefits
  • Start date: As soon as possible
  • Contract duration: Fixed term until 29 February 2028
  • Extension: Subject to funding availability
  • Posting date: 23 July 2026
  • Application deadline: 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST
  • Office requirement: At least three days per week
  • Work-authorisation requirement: Right to live and work in the United Kingdom

About the Center for Global Development

The Center for Global Development, commonly known as CGD, is an independent, non-partisan and nonprofit policy research organisation with offices in Washington, DC, and London.

CGD conducts empirical research on policies, institutions and financial decisions that affect low- and middle-income countries. Its work examines how governments, international organisations, corporations, development agencies and financial institutions can contribute to more inclusive and sustainable development.

The organisation combines research with engagement across the global policy community. Rather than producing analysis solely for academic audiences, CGD seeks to translate research findings into practical recommendations that can influence development policy, financing and implementation.

Its work often sits at the intersection of:

  • Development economics
  • Public policy
  • International finance
  • Aid effectiveness
  • Global institutions
  • Poverty reduction
  • Evidence-based decision-making
  • Development cooperation

The Research Analyst will support this wider mission by contributing to work on how development organisations identify, assess and use evidence about cost-effective interventions.

About the Smart Buys Alliance

The Smart Buys Alliance connects development agencies, philanthropic organisations and research institutions seeking to increase investment in effective development interventions.

The alliance promotes the use of evidence when governments and donors decide how to allocate limited development resources. Its work is particularly concerned with identifying interventions that can produce substantial positive outcomes relative to their costs.

The alliance operates through three principal areas of work.

Developing On-Demand Smart Buy Lists

The Smart Buys Alliance supports the development of lists identifying development interventions with strong evidence of cost-effectiveness.

These resources are intended to help funders and policymakers compare options and direct resources toward programmes that are likely to deliver significant results.

Supporting Implementation and Evidence Building

Identifying an effective intervention is only one part of the process. The alliance also supports implementation and encourages donors to coordinate their efforts to strengthen the evidence base.

This may involve examining how interventions perform in different settings, identifying implementation constraints and understanding whether the results of one programme can be reproduced elsewhere.

Convening a Community of Practice

The alliance brings together policymakers, researchers, funders and development practitioners to exchange evidence, experience and practical lessons.

The Smart Buys Alliance is a collaboration involving:

  • Center for Effective Global Action
  • Cooperation Globale
  • Center for Global Development
  • Global Poverty Research Lab
  • Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab
  • Participating donor agencies and partners

The Research Analyst will support CGD’s contribution to this partnership.

Purpose of the Research Analyst Position

The Research Analyst will provide analytical, operational and administrative support to CGD’s Smart Buys Alliance work.

The role is intended to help the project deliver accurate, timely and policy-relevant research outputs. It is not limited to data analysis: the selected candidate will also contribute to writing, coordination, stakeholder engagement and the organisation of policy events.

The Research Analyst will report to Michelle Rao, Fellow at CGD Europe, and work closely with members of the broader research team.

The role requires someone who can move comfortably between detailed analytical work and practical project coordination. On one day, the Analyst may be cleaning a dataset or reviewing causal-inference evidence; on another, they may be revising a policy report, coordinating a roundtable or arranging travel for project partners.

Research and Analytical Responsibilities

Analysing Donor Use of Cost-Effectiveness Evidence

A major component of the role will involve examining how donor agencies engage with and use evidence about cost-effective development interventions.

The Research Analyst may help investigate questions such as:

  • How do donor agencies define cost-effectiveness?
  • What evidence do they use when selecting interventions?
  • How consistently is evidence incorporated into funding decisions?
  • What organisational factors encourage or prevent evidence use?
  • How can the use of cost-effectiveness evidence be monitored?
  • How might donor practices change over time?

Work in this area may include:

  • Literature reviews
  • Data collection
  • Data extraction
  • Dataset construction
  • Data cleaning
  • Quantitative analysis
  • Textual analysis
  • Review of policy and organisational documents

Textual Analysis Using Large Language Models

The position may involve using large language models to support the analysis of textual data.

This could include examining development strategies, policy documents, donor reports or other materials to identify patterns in how organisations discuss and apply evidence.

Candidates with prior experience using large language models for evidence synthesis or textual analysis will have an advantage. However, this experience is identified as beneficial rather than mandatory.

Applicants should understand that the role requires analytical judgement. Tools may assist with large volumes of text, but conclusions must still be transparent, credible and suitable for policy research.

Research on Evidence Use in Development Policy

The Research Analyst will support wider research on how evidence informs international development policy.

This may include:

  • Original data analysis
  • Quantitative research
  • Cost-effectiveness analysis
  • Heterogeneity analysis
  • Causal-inference methods
  • Evidence synthesis
  • Interpretation of empirical findings
  • Preparation of charts and visualisations

Heterogeneity analysis may be used to examine whether an intervention produces different effects across populations, countries or implementation settings.

Cost-effectiveness analysis may involve comparing the costs and outcomes of different interventions to assess which approaches offer greater value.

Drafting Research Outputs

The Research Analyst will contribute to drafting and revising:

  • Academic or policy papers
  • Research reports
  • Policy briefs
  • Blogs
  • Monitoring products
  • Analytical summaries
  • Supporting materials for stakeholders

The selected candidate must be able to communicate technical findings clearly without flattening the nuance out of them. Policy audiences generally need clarity, not a statistical fog bank.

The Analyst will work under the guidance of the Research Fellow and in collaboration with the wider research team.

Monitoring Evidence-Use Initiatives

The role also involves tracking initiatives intended to increase the use of evidence by:

  • Development organisations
  • Bilateral agencies
  • Governments
  • Donor institutions
  • Research organisations

This may require maintaining structured records, following institutional developments and synthesising information from multiple organisations or processes.

Convenings and Policy-Engagement Responsibilities

Research is only useful when it reaches the people making decisions. The Research Analyst will therefore contribute to workshops, roundtables and other policy-engagement activities.

Planning Events

The successful candidate will support the planning and organisation of:

  • Workshops
  • Roundtable discussions
  • Research launches
  • Partner meetings
  • Policy events
  • Stakeholder consultations

Responsibilities may include preparing timelines, maintaining participant lists, coordinating invitations and ensuring that logistical arrangements are completed.

Meeting Coordination

The role requires coordinating meetings among participants based in different countries and time zones.

The Research Analyst may need to:

  • Identify suitable time-zone options
  • Liaise with participants
  • Manage calendars
  • Confirm attendance
  • Circulate meeting materials
  • Maintain schedules
  • Follow up on agreed actions

Strong attention to detail is important because international coordination has a peculiar ability to turn one missing calendar invitation into a minor diplomatic incident.

Travel Arrangements

The Research Analyst will support travel planning for partners and participants attending Smart Buys Alliance events.

This may include coordinating itineraries, gathering traveller information and communicating logistical arrangements.

Required Academic Qualifications

Applicants must hold a master’s degree in one of the following areas:

  • Economics
  • Public policy
  • International development
  • Development economics
  • A closely related discipline

The position requires advanced analytical training, particularly because the successful candidate will work with empirical research, quantitative methods and policy evidence.

Required Professional Experience

Candidates must have at least four years of professional experience in economic or public-policy analysis related to international development.

Relevant experience may have been gained in:

  • Policy research organisations
  • Universities
  • International organisations
  • Government institutions
  • Development agencies
  • Think tanks
  • Consulting organisations
  • NGOs
  • Philanthropic foundations

Applicants should demonstrate meaningful responsibility for analytical work rather than only general exposure to development projects.

Research and Quantitative Skills

Candidates must have strong research and quantitative analytical skills.

They should have experience designing and conducting empirical research in an academic or professional environment.

Expected capabilities include:

  • Structuring research questions
  • Reviewing relevant literature
  • Working with quantitative datasets
  • Cleaning and validating data
  • Applying appropriate analytical methods
  • Interpreting findings
  • Communicating limitations
  • Producing credible research outputs

Knowledge of causal-inference methods is required.

This may include familiarity with methods used to estimate the effects of programmes or policies and distinguish causal relationships from simple correlations.

Required and Desirable Software Skills

Applicants should be able to conduct quantitative analysis and produce visualisations using:

  • R
  • Stata

Experience with the following is an advantage:

  • Python
  • Git
  • Large language models
  • Textual-analysis tools
  • Evidence-synthesis methods

Candidates should explain how they have used relevant tools in actual research rather than merely listing software names in their CV.

Writing and Communication Skills

Excellent written communication is required.

The successful applicant must be able to summarise complicated empirical findings clearly and concisely for policy audiences.

Strong candidates will demonstrate the ability to:

  • Write logically structured research outputs
  • Explain quantitative findings in accessible language
  • Distinguish evidence from interpretation
  • Tailor writing to different audiences
  • Revise work in response to feedback
  • Maintain accuracy while remaining concise

Applicants must submit a writing sample, making the quality and relevance of that document particularly important.

Organisational and Coordination Experience

Candidates should have experience supporting:

  • Committees
  • Working groups
  • Research partnerships
  • Multi-stakeholder processes
  • Cross-institutional initiatives

Experience in professional communications, social-media management or event coordination is also relevant.

The role requires a person who can manage research responsibilities alongside operational tasks without allowing either side of the job to drift into chaos.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate:

  • High attention to detail
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines
  • Strong calendar and scheduling skills
  • Experience maintaining shared documents
  • Clear and reliable communication
  • Ability to coordinate across institutions
  • Confidence working across time zones

Collaboration and Working Style

The Research Analyst will work with colleagues and partners from several institutions.

CGD is seeking someone with a collaborative and team-oriented working style who can contribute effectively across organisational boundaries.

The successful candidate should be able to:

  • Work independently when necessary
  • Seek guidance appropriately
  • Share information with colleagues
  • Respond constructively to feedback
  • Coordinate with external partners
  • Adapt to changing project priorities
  • Maintain professional relationships across institutions

Salary and Benefits

The annual salary range is:

£46,725–£51,187

The appointment also includes excellent benefits, although the vacancy information provided does not list the individual benefit components.

The exact salary offered within the range will likely depend on the successful candidate’s experience and qualifications.

Contract Duration and Start Date

The successful candidate is expected to begin as soon as possible.

The position is fixed term and will run until:

29 February 2028

An extension may be possible if additional funding becomes available. Applicants should not assume that an extension is guaranteed.

London-Based Hybrid Working Arrangement

The position is based in London.

The successful candidate must live within commutable distance of CGD’s offices in the SW1 area and attend the office at least three days per week.

The position should therefore not be treated as a fully remote opportunity.

Applicants should consider the practical implications of commuting to central London before applying.

Right-to-Work Requirement

Candidates must already have, or be able to obtain, the legal right to live and work in the United Kingdom.

The vacancy does not state that visa sponsorship will be provided.

Applicants requiring sponsorship should confirm the organisation’s policy before relying on this position as a route to UK work authorisation.

Application Requirements

Interested candidates must submit:

  1. A current CV
  2. A cover letter
  3. A writing sample

Preparing the CV

The CV should clearly demonstrate:

  • Relevant academic qualifications
  • At least four years of applicable experience
  • Quantitative research responsibilities
  • Experience with R and Stata
  • Knowledge of causal-inference methods
  • Policy-writing experience
  • Coordination or event-management responsibilities

Preparing the Cover Letter

The cover letter should explain how the applicant meets the position’s requirements.

Candidates should provide specific examples of:

  • Empirical research they have conducted
  • Development-policy questions they have analysed
  • Datasets they have cleaned or managed
  • Quantitative methods they have applied
  • Research they have translated for policy audiences
  • Multi-stakeholder processes they have supported
  • Competing deadlines they have successfully managed

Selecting a Writing Sample

The writing sample should demonstrate the ability to communicate research clearly.

A strong sample may include:

  • A policy brief
  • A research report
  • An analytical blog
  • An academic paper section
  • A development-policy publication

Applicants should choose a sample that reflects their own contribution and is relevant to the role.

Manual Application Review

CGD states that applications will be reviewed manually.

No artificial-intelligence system or automated filter will be used to screen applicants.

Candidates should still tailor their materials carefully, but they do not need to construct their CV around an imaginary robot guarding the door with a keyword clipboard.

Equal Opportunity Statement

CGD Europe is an equal-opportunity employer committed to a collaborative, diverse and inclusive workplace.

Applicants will be considered without discrimination based on characteristics including:

  • Race
  • Colour
  • Creed
  • National origin
  • Ancestry
  • Gender
  • Gender identity or expression
  • Parental status
  • Veteran status
  • Marital status
  • Disability
  • Religious affiliation
  • Political affiliation
  • Age
  • Sexual orientation

Selection will be based on the requirements of the position and the applicant’s qualifications and experience.

Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by:

6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST

Candidates should submit before the closing time to avoid last-minute technical problems.

International applicants should note that the deadline is stated in British Summer Time.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The CGD Research Analyst position offers an experienced international-development researcher the opportunity to contribute to influential work on cost-effectiveness and evidence use in development policy.

The role combines quantitative research, policy writing, large-scale textual analysis, coordination and stakeholder engagement. It is especially suited to candidates who can move confidently between data, ideas and the practical machinery of international collaboration.

Applicants need a relevant master’s degree, at least four years of professional experience, strong quantitative skills and experience using R and Stata. Knowledge of causal inference is required, while experience with Python, Git, evidence synthesis or large language models would strengthen an application.

The position is based in London, offers a salary of £46,725–£51,187, and will continue until 29 February 2028, with a possible extension depending on funding.

Qualified candidates must submit their CV, cover letter and writing sample by 6 August 2026 at 5:00 PM BST.
